title: AI Stocks Are Falling. Dan Ives Says It’s Just Getting Started.
creator: MarketBeat
summary: MarketBeat, partnering with Matt Weinschenk from Top Stocks, interviews Dan Ives on the state of the AI bull market — the same interview previously posted on 16 October and analyzed as video Z5gI10nu3Pk, republished here under a new title as AI stocks fall. Ives argues the AI party started at 9:30pm, is now at about 11:30pm and runs to roughly 4am: investors are, in his view, less than 15% through the coming AI spending, with an $8–10 multiplier across tech for every $1 spent on an Nvidia chip, and two to three more years of tech bull market. On AI safety and possible slowdowns he says technology always outruns regulation, self-regulation is the likely path, and slowing down hands the lead to China; safety itself is a growth area, including cybersecurity and sovereign AI. He discusses Palantir and Nvidia on sovereign AI, Meta's Muse assistant and its 3.5 billion-user install base, hyperscaler monetisation inflecting at Microsoft, Google and Amazon, neo-clouds Nebius and CoreWeave, Tesla's six-to-nine-month robotaxi and Optimus pivot and a more-than-80% chance of a Tesla–SpaceX merger by end-2027, Apple's new AI strategy, and AMD as a major player under Lisa Su. The hosts note Apple and Microsoft sit in Ives's top-10 stocks to buy, but Ives states no explicit buy, hold or sell call, price or target for any ticker in the interview, so all entries are logged UNCERTAIN and no stance flip is recorded. Auto-captions garble several names, including Nebius, Palantir and Ives himself.
